original_question: For n >= 1, let B_n denote the metric completion of the universal metric covering of the configuration space W_n = {(z_1, ..., z_n) in C^n : z_i != z_j for i != j}, equivalently the universal covering of C^n infinitely branching along the hyperplanes z_i = z_j, equipped with the lifted length metric. Is B_n a CAT(0) space for every n?
target_in_paper: Section 2, "Braid space" — the paper's unnumbered open problem asking whether the braid space associated to the diagonals z_i=z_j in \mathbb{C}^n is CAT(0) for all n. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2510.11908v1))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right object, the right metric construction, and the right question: the paper defines the braid space via infinite branching along the complex hyperplanes z_i=z_j and, equivalently, as the completion of the universal metric covering of the complement of those hyperplanes, then asks whether it is CAT(0) for any n. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2510.11908v1))
missing_details: State explicitly that W_n is given the path metric induced from the standard Euclidean metric on \mathbb{C}^n; the paper says \mathbb{C}^n has its canonical Euclidean metric and the braid space has the lifted length metric.
Spell out the branch locus as the complex hyperplanes H_{ij}=\{z_i=z_j\} for 1<=i<j<=n; this is the paper's geometric description before the W_n reformulation.
If you want the question to reflect the paper's nearby context, note separately that the cases n<=3 are already known; the genuinely open part is the general n case.
The symbols W_n and B_n are convenient and mathematically accurate, but Section 2 itself speaks simply of "the braid space" rather than introducing those symbols.
refined_question: For each integer n>=2, let H_n=\bigcup_{1\le i<j\le n}\{(z_1,\dots,z_n)\in\mathbb{C}^n:z_i=z_j\}, let W_n=\mathbb{C}^n\setminus H_n with the path metric induced by the standard Euclidean metric on \mathbb{C}^n, and let B_n be the metric completion of the universal metric covering of W_n. Is B_n a CAT(0) space for every n?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, equip \mathbb{C}^n with its canonical Euclidean metric and let B_n denote the universal cover of \mathbb{C}^n infinitely branched along the complex hyperplanes z_i=z_j for 1\le i<j\le n, endowed with the lifted length metric. Is B_n CAT(0) for every n?
justification: The exact target is the unnumbered open problem in Section 2, "Braid space." This paper is a gallery of problems rather than a theorem/conjecture paper with a Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3 chain, and your draft is already very close to the official formulation. The refinements above only make the ambient Euclidean metric and the branch locus explicit, while keeping the scope exactly at the CAT(0) question for this braid space. The paper also records that the answer is known for n<=3, which is useful context but not part of the question itself. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2510.11908v1))
